title: What can be done with a dead body?
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss what can be done with a dead body: cremains turned into synthetic diamonds (LifeGem), cremains shot into space, the Afterlife Project microbial fuel cell grave marker that generates power from decomposition, green burials (biodegradable caskets, eco pods, bamboo, dry ice instead of embalming fluid, conservation burial land easements, cremains in artificial reef), cremation energy recovery in Sweden, and alkaline hydrolysis (resomation) and the proposed New York bill nicknamed the "Hannibal Lecter bill." Includes some joking banter about their own preferred ways to go.
topics: what can be done with a dead body

segments.title: Opening banter and Hunter S. Thompson
segments.summary: Hosts joke about being shot out of a cannon, referencing Hunter S. Thompson's ashes fired from a cannon in Woody Creek, Colorado, and Josh's own joking idea of a body left for carrion crows.

segments.title: Cremains into diamonds and space
segments.summary: Discussion of LifeGem, which compresses a portion of cremated remains into a synthetic diamond, and of shooting ashes into space, including Timothy Leary's flight and the affordable suborbital options.

segments.title: The Afterlife Project
segments.summary: Describes a conceptual art project in which a microbial fuel cell beneath a decomposing body converts gastric decomposition products into electricity to power devices via a grave marker; the hosts note it was meant as a proof-of-concept.

segments.title: Green burial movement and traditional burial problems
segments.summary: Discusses a survey of people over fifty interested in green burials, the environmental harm of embalming fluid and traditional caskets, and the historical practice of sitting up with the dead before embalming.

segments.title: Greener caskets, cremation, and Swedish crematorium heat
segments.summary: Covers biodegradable options such as bamboo caskets and eco pods made of recycled newspaper, dry ice refrigeration in place of formaldehyde, concerns about groundwater near cemeteries, and Sweden's crematoriums supplying heat to homes.

segments.title: Alkaline hydrolysis, conservation burial, and other options
segments.summary: Describes alkaline hydrolysis, which dissolves a body in lye under heat and pressure, and the New York funeral director's effort to legalize it, which opponents dubbed the Hannibal Lecter bill. Also covers conservation burial land easements, cremains in artificial reefs, and a closing plug for related articles.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts point listeners to related HowStuffWorks articles and sign off.
